external_relations.target_title: Gate: observe complete K4 xtmux and Specialists change sets
K4-Core — Complete lifecycle, managed distribution, and required policies
External gate observation — programme GATE-IFACE passed

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Codex is not yet a first-class XTRM interactive runtime. The existing epic mixed a correct capability corpus with a provisional linear Track A–G sequence, optional MCP/plugin work, broad Serena cleanup, and xtmux domain language that could imply duplicate authorities.

## SUCCESS
Deliver behavioral parity for Codex through the canonical K0–K7 graph. K0–K2 establish freshness, Pi/Claude characterization, real Codex payload fixtures, and a generic deterministic launcher/outcome spine. K3 then produces three experimental repository-owned vertical slices. K4 completes required lifecycle, distribution, configuration ownership, policy, and recovery work. Production promotion K5 requires both K4 and the already-passed programme GATE-IFACE. K6 releases in dependency-safe order. K7 holds optional capabilities.

## SCOPE
Core is the lead repository and owns launcher contracts, interactive worktrees, installation, managed AGENTS/skills/.codex configuration, safety profiles, exact resume, diagnostics, release integration, and the coordinated smoke. xtmux and Specialists execute through companion roots in their own Beads databases. Jira KAN-127 is a coordination mirror only.

## NON_GOALS
Do not make xt codex a prerequisite of I1.4 or GATE-IFACE. Do not depend on ResolvedChain, specialists.execution.v1, the chain reducer, or C1/D1/E1. Do not require MCP or plugin packaging for minimum parity. Do not reimplement xtmux messages, obligations, monitors, wakes, identity, or scheduling. Do not make complete historical Serena cleanup block the first vertical slice. Do not create cross-repository parent-child trees.

## CONSTRAINTS
Behavioral parity is not asset parity. Core, xtmux, Specialists, Beads, and Git keep their existing authorities. Codex uses a distinct runtime descriptor. The managed default is YOLO; --no-yolo selects workspace-write with on-request approval. Neither profile may bypass hook trust. Managed .codex operations must preserve unowned content. One operation has one worktree owner. All exact design references must use repository-resolvable, commit-pinned links.

## VALIDATION
Pi/Claude characterization fixtures prove the generic launcher/outcome contract. Real installed-version Codex payload fixtures prove adapters. Each repository validates its own implementation and negative ownership boundaries. K5 runs the cross-repository parity matrix only after GATE-IFACE. K6 ends with a smoke against installed, compatible package releases.

## OUTPUT
Repository-local K0–K7 Beads with explicit local dependencies and external companion/gate references; backward-compatible releases in the order contract-only Core if required, xtmux and Specialists, Core launcher, then released-trio smoke. Canonical sequencing note: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/xtrm/blob/ed06ba222307030c7153c43cd2370262706b78a4/docs/shared/xtrm-codex-kan-127-execution-note.md
source.notes:
Scoped audit of the three original ~/dev/xtrm/docs/shared documents (no edits; programme docs remain owned elsewhere): (1) xtrm-cli-actionable-outcomes-and-followups.md is explicitly a 2026-07-24 proposal and its candidate nested _outcome shape/status vocabulary is not the merged Core K2 top-level CommandOutcomeV1; it must be marked historical or reconciled before being treated as current contract. (2) xtrm-harness-native-adapters.md still describes MCP 2026-07-28 as release-candidate despite its own inserted warning that MCP 2.0 shipped; all Claude MCP/Tasks assumptions require freshness review. (3) xtrm-native-pi-tools-pi-extensible-workflows-integration-2026-07-30.md links two obsolete filenames that do not exist in docs/shared. The directory now has eight files, not three, because xtrm PR #31 added four plan/reconciliation artifacts and PR #32 added the KAN-127 note. KAN-127 work must use the commit-pinned PR #32 note and merged Core K2 as authority, not these proposal details.

=== HANDOFF TO THE SERVER LANE (written 2026-08-07 by the local lane) ===

READ THIS BEFORE RE-PLANNING. Your last recorded position (KAN-127 comment of 2026-08-04) is stale in three specific ways: it says xtmux K4 is "Not started", Specialists #248 is open, and xtmux #93 is open. All three are now false. The authoritative cross-repo evidence is the close reason on xtrm-ozknq.15 — read that first.

WHAT LANDED WHILE YOU WERE OUT
- xtmux #93 merged 8f7f997d; Specialists #248 merged 7053236f.
- xtmux-s96.2.1 (compatibility-link adoption) merged as xtmux #94 / 0560b7de.
- Core #542 merged dd937514 — Specialists vendor pin refreshed from the stale c1e660ab to the immutable 7053236f. This was a precondition written into xtrm-ozknq.15's own notes and was not in your plan.
- xtmux-s96.4 (K4-xtmux) built, verified and merged as xtmux #96 / 8ff2c074. CLOSED.
- xtrm-ozknq.15 CLOSED. xtrm-codex-giface CLOSED — KAN-127 is resolvable at xtrmxt.atlassian.net (id 10587); the 2026-08-02 zero-result was a lookup against the wrong Atlassian cloud, not a missing issue.

K4 is therefore COMPLETE in all three repositories.

DO NOT RESUME AS CO-COORDINATOR ON .10/.11/.12
We already collided once: you ran K1 concurrently with this lane and closed its claims mid-flight. On a merge that was recoverable. What remains is not:
- .11 (K5) is a single promotion decision; two actors cannot both take it.
- .12 + xtmux-s96.5 + unitAI-e67up.5 are an ORDERED release wave under the rule "never publish a repository that depends on an unpublished sibling surface". A publish is not revertible.
- .10 is one signed-off evidence packet with one owner.
Single-writer for all of these.

WHERE YOU ARE GENUINELY USEFUL — SECOND-HOST PARITY EVIDENCE
K1 established that Codex hook trust is PER-HOST, and that on the audit host the installed xtmux Codex hooks were inert because trust had never been granted, making any lifecycle capability measured before the grant invalid evidence. Trust state must be confirmed per host before any parity claim. The VPS is therefore a real second data point for xtrm-ozknq.10, not duplicated effort. Same for the packaging leg: .10 wants package-compatibility evidence and a second machine installing from packed tarballs is genuine coverage.
Caveat for that work: installed @jaggerxtrm/specialists 3.21.2 has NO launch-outcome verb and no --surface codex, so package-compatibility evidence must come from source checkouts or locally packed tarballs, not the published packages, until K6 ships.

ALSO AVAILABLE AND SELF-CONTAINED
A specialists-repo PR for four beads-hook fixes currently carried only in ~/.claude/hooks/ on the local host, which die on the next `specialists install`:
 1. epic exemption in the stop and commit gates (an open programme epic otherwise blocks every commit and session close in the repo);
 2. beads-commit-gate.mjs resolving the beads DB from the SESSION cwd, so a commit in a sibling checkout is gated on another repo's open work — now resolves the command's target path;
 3. beads-stop-gate.mjs attributing work by session (partial — see below);
 4. NOT FIXED: the commit gate substring-matches a commit invocation anywhere in the command string, so even a `bd remember` whose quoted TEXT contains that phrase is blocked as though it were a real commit.
On (3): the attribution compares issue started_at against the transcript birthtime. That is unsound for long-running sessions — the local session's transcript was born 2026-08-02, so another lane's bead created 2026-08-06 still reads as in-session. The correct fix is explicit claim recording (a claimed:<session_id> key written at claim time, read at Stop); the Pi extension writes such a key but nothing does for Claude Code sessions. Treat the shipped heuristic as partial.

BEFORE YOU START
Check the VPS for unpushed branches or local commits. You stopped mid-task with a failing local suite while both of your pushed PRs were already green and the CodeQL condition you were waiting on had passed — so verify against origin before landing anything, in case it is already superseded.

OPEN, IN ORDER: xtrm-ozknq.10 (ready) -> .11 (K5) -> xtmux-s96.5 + unitAI-e67up.5 -> .17 -> .12 -> .13 (K7, optional).

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Repository-local green tests do not prove that Core, xtmux, and Specialists agree on identity, lifecycle, safety, configuration ownership, and recovery.

## SUCCESS
Run the Codex-specific parity matrix against the stable generic contracts after all three K4 change sets are complete. Produce immutable evidence for K5.

## SCOPE
Covers Core xtrm-ozknq.9, xtmux xtmux-s96.4, and Specialists unitAI-e67up.4. Exercise identity correlation, exact resume, YOLO/--no-yolo, hook trust, managed config preservation, roles, messages, obligations, waits, replies, recovery, cleanup, and package compatibility.

## NON_GOALS
Do not authorize production support, publish packages, require optional MCP/plugin capabilities, or alter GATE-IFACE.

## CONSTRAINTS
Use compatible repository versions or packed artifacts. Use real installed-version Codex fixtures. Keep repository authority boundaries observable. Redact payloads and credentials.

## VALIDATION
Fail on identity mismatch, prose parsing, false readiness, leaked worktrees, wrong resume thread, hook-trust bypass, destructive config cleanup, duplicate coordination authority, missing role/result behavior, or Pi/Claude regression.

## OUTPUT
A signed-off parity evidence packet that blocks K5 until green and records exact package/commit versions.
source.title: Test: K4 cross-repository Codex parity matrix — contract, lifecycle, and pre-release smoke

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Experimental slices and green repository tests must not be mistaken for a production compatibility promise before the generic interface gate and Codex-specific matrix both pass.

## SUCCESS
Authorize production-supported xt codex only when programme GATE-IFACE is already passed and xtrm-ozknq.10 is green against the stable contracts.

## SCOPE
A release decision gate for Codex-specific parity. Confirm required evidence, compatible versions, remaining limits, and operator documentation.

## NON_GOALS
Do not implement missing features inside the gate, waive failed fixtures, depend on C1/D1/E1, or authorize K7 capabilities.

## CONSTRAINTS
GATE-IFACE is external and is proven through Pi/Claude plus the generic contract; it does not depend on production xt codex. This bead cannot close while either prerequisite is unresolved.

## VALIDATION
Review the K2 contract approval, GATE-IFACE evidence, Pi/Claude regressions, three-repository K4 completion, parity matrix, hook trust, ownership preservation, failure cleanup, and compatible package plan.

## OUTPUT
An explicit promote/reject decision. Promotion unblocks ordered sibling and Core releases; rejection creates scoped repository-local follow-ups without weakening the gate.
source.title: K5 — Promote Codex parity after programme GATE-IFACE

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Publishing Core before compatible xtmux and Specialists versions would create an unpublished cross-repository dependency and an untestable installation state.

## SUCCESS
After K5, consume the published backward-compatible xtmux and Specialists compatibility versions, publish the Core launcher/integration release, and pass a coordinated smoke of all three installed packages with Codex.

## SCOPE
Core version/compatibility pins, changelog, package publication, install/update diagnostics, operator docs, and final released-trio smoke. A prior contract-only Core release is permitted only if K2 required packaged schema publication.

## NON_GOALS
Do not reorder releases, test branch-only siblings, add K7 features, or silently broaden parity requirements.

## CONSTRAINTS
Release order is contract-only Core if needed; xtmux and Specialists in parallel; Core launcher; then installed-trio smoke. Every dependency must refer to a published version.

## VALIDATION
Verify package contents, compatibility metadata, clean global install, idempotent update, drift repair, exact launch/resume/end, role invocation/results, xtmux coordination/recovery, unowned config preservation, and no source-path leakage.

## OUTPUT
Published compatible Core, xtmux, and Specialists versions plus immutable smoke evidence and refreshed current operator documentation.
source.title: K6-Core — Release the launcher after sibling compatibility versions and run released-trio smoke

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Useful Codex-native extensions exist, but mixing them into minimum parity would delay the supported vertical slice and obscure ownership.

## SUCCESS
Hold optional follow-ups until K6 is complete and measured operator need justifies a repository-owned child.

## SCOPE
Potential plugin packaging, managed MCP bundle, review/structured-exec products, browser/apps/connectors/goals, direct Codex Specialist backend, and expanded quality/memory/debug adapters.

## NON_GOALS
Do not claim or implement follow-ups before K6. Do not retrofit optional work into K0–K5 acceptance or weaken one-authority boundaries.

## CONSTRAINTS
Each future follow-up must have evidence of operator value, one repository owner, independent acceptance, backward-compatible contracts, and no native Codex subagent dependency.

## VALIDATION
Before creating a follow-up, record the measured gap, current native capability, ownership decision, security/trust implications, and why existing XTRM authorities cannot already provide the outcome.

## OUTPUT
A blocked optional-capability holding task. It becomes claimable only after the released parity smoke; each accepted capability receives a separately scoped repository-local issue.
source.title: K7 — Optional Codex capabilities after parity release

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Core K6 must not publish the launcher while sibling compatibility work exists only in branches or unpublished packages.

## SUCCESS
Close this observation gate only after xtmux xtmux-s96.5 and Specialists unitAI-e67up.5 have published backward-compatible versions authorized by K5.

## SCOPE
Release evidence and compatible-version verification only. This gate depends locally on K5 and blocks the Core launcher release.

## NON_GOALS
Do not publish sibling packages from Core, reorder the release wave, or accept branch-only dependencies.

## CONSTRAINTS
Record registry versions, release commits, package contents, compatibility metadata, and post-publish checks. A contract-only Core release may precede this gate only when K2 required it.

## VALIDATION
Install both published sibling versions against the supported Core line and verify their focused compatibility suites before closing.

## OUTPUT
A manual release synchronization acknowledgement consumed by Core K6.
